subject: Cost-routing across free and cheap agent models with a hard quality-ceiling boundary

cases.scenario: An agent plans to grade a batch of eval responses (assigning quality verdicts) using a free/cheap model 'to save cost,' reasoning that grading is mechanical-ish and a free model can handle it.
cases.context: The grader's verdicts become the quality signal that downstream decisions are built on.
cases.question: Is a free model appropriate for this work, and how should it be routed?
expected_flags: Grading / eval scoring / quality verdicts are quality-judging work — a weak judge silently poisons every downstream decision built on its verdicts
This is the hard boundary: quality-creating and quality-judging work never goes to a free/cheap model, regardless of cost
expected_fix_hints: Route the grading to a frontier model — never a free/cheap one
Treat the cost saving as illusory when the output is the quality bar
absent_signals: Do not route grading/eval scoring to a free or cheap model to save cost
Do not claim retrying a free model enough makes it a valid judge

cases.scenario: A job is a deterministic bulk rename + format pass across many files, and a teammate wants to send it to a frontier model 'to be safe.'
cases.context: The work involves no reasoning; a script could arguably do most of it.
cases.question: Where should this work be routed and why?
expected_flags: Deterministic/mechanical work needs no reasoning; routing it to a frontier model wastes premium capacity
A script is the first choice; otherwise the cheapest free model clears this low per-item bar
expected_fix_hints: Do it with a script first; else route to the cheapest free model (GPT-5 Nano-class)
Do not escalate to a frontier model merely because one is available
absent_signals: Do not route deterministic mechanical work to a frontier model by default
Do not treat 'a frontier model is available' as a reason to escalate

cases.scenario: A large-context agentic coding task on a big repo needs a free model with both frontier-band coding ability and a huge context window.
cases.context: The task is genuine agentic coding over a large codebase; the team wants to stay on the free lane if a model clears the bar.
cases.question: Which free model best fits, and what is its tradeoff?
expected_flags: MiniMax M3 Free is the strongest free default for large-context coding — frontier-band coding plus a 1M-token context window
It is the highest-capability free lane for this shape of work
expected_fix_hints: Route the large-context coding to MiniMax M3 Free
Confirm the live free roster before relying on it (`opencode models opencode`)
absent_signals: Do not route this to a low-ceiling nano-class model
Do not assume any free model clears the large-context coding bar

cases.scenario: A free model assigned to a triage job starts looping without progress and returns a contradictory, low-confidence result. The operator's instinct is to keep retrying the same free model until it converges.
cases.context: The free model is showing concrete failure signals; the task has not crossed into quality-judging.
cases.question: What should the operator do, and what is the rule for escalating?
expected_flags: Looping without progress, self-contradiction, and a low-confidence/malformed result are concrete escalation signals
Retrying cannot raise a model above its ceiling — these signals mean promote the work, not retry harder
expected_fix_hints: Escalate this work to a frontier model on the concrete failure signal
Escalate on signal (looping/contradiction/low-confidence/scope crossing), not merely because a frontier model is available
absent_signals: Do not keep retrying the same free model past a clear failure signal
Do not escalate by default in the absence of any signal

cases.scenario: A high-volume bulk classification/extraction lane needs throughput with a capped thinking budget, where each item's quality bar is low.
cases.context: The per-item bar is low; the lane is background and volume-bound.
cases.question: Which free model family fits this lane?
expected_flags: High-throughput reasoning with a capped thinking budget (Nemotron-class) fits a volume triage/extraction lane
It is a throughput choice, not the top-end coding choice
expected_fix_hints: Route the bulk triage/extraction to a high-throughput free model (Nemotron-class)
Match the per-item bar to the model ceiling rather than picking purely on cost
absent_signals: Do not route correctness-critical synthesis to a throughput-tuned model
Do not assume throughput implies top-end coding ability

cases.scenario: A user asks: 'How do I invoke OpenCode non-interactively from a script, and how do I structure the retry/claim logic for my autonomous agent loop?'
cases.context: The first question is about operating the OpenCode runtime; the second is about authoring the agent loop's control flow. Neither is a per-task free-model choice.
cases.question: How should the agent scope this request?
expected_flags: Invoking/operating the OpenCode runtime is owned by the opencode skill, not this model-choice skill
Authoring the agent loop's retry/claim/escalation control flow is owned by the autonomous-loop-patterns skill
expected_fix_hints: Route the runtime-invocation question to the opencode skill
Route the loop-authoring question to the autonomous-loop-patterns skill

Do not treat agent-loop authoring as within this skill's scope
